newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AMBROSE PLUNGES AUSTRALIA INTO CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE PLUNGES AUSTRALIA INTO CRISIS.

text.p: West Indies fast-bowler Curtly Ambrose plunged Australia into crisis on Saturday by ripping through the top order for the second time in the third test.
Ambrose, who took five wickets in Australia's first innings, removed opener Matthew Hayden and number three Justin Langer for ducks at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
At lunch on the third day, Australia were in deep trouble at 41 for three, a lead of five runs, after being reduced to three for two in the third over.
Australia, who lead the five-test series 2-0, suffered a major blow just before lunch when captain and opener Mark Taylor lost his wicket for 10, extending a run of low scores.
West Indies earlier added 22 runs to their overnight total before losing their last wicket to be dismissed for 255, a lead of 36 runs on Australia's first innings 219.
Left-hander Jimmy Adams, batting at number six, remained unbeaten on 74 after West Indies captain and fast-bowler Courtney Walsh was dismissed for four by leg-spinner Shane Warne.
Mark Waugh survived a nervous hour before lunch to remain on 19 not out alongside his brother Steve Waugh on six.
Hayden was bowled in the first over of the innings without playing a shot to a straight ball that clipped his off stump.
Langer fell two overs later when he attempted a pull shot only to deflect the ball off the back of his bat to Carl Hooper at second slip.
